newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan president exonerated in Murtaza killing.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan president exonerated in Murtaza killing.

text.p: A Pakistani judicial tribunal has exonerated President Farooq Leghari of involvement in the killing of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza Bhutto, an official said on Sunday.
The tribunal's report, made public on Sunday, rejected Bhutto's allegation that her brother's murder was a conspiracy hatched by Leghari to dislodge her government, he said.
It described Murtaza's death as an "extra-judicial killing" and said police should not have obeyed what it called Bhutto's "illegal" orders when she was prime minister.
Leghari dismissed Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.

The three-member tribunal was set up on October 18 under Justice Nasir Aslam Zahid, a Supreme Court judge, to probe the death of Murtaza, killed with seven companions by police bullets on September 20 near his home in the southern city of Karachi.
Police said on Sunday they had detained Karachi's former deputy inspector general of police, a suspect in the killing.
"Shoaib Suddle has been detained," a senior police officer said, without specifying the reason. "His residence has been declared as a sub-jail after his detention overnight."
Suddle was staying at the Police Club in Karachi's affluent Defence Society suburb.

Police have accused Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari, former chief minister of Sindh province Abdullah Shah, former Intelligence Bureau chief Masood Sharif and 19 police officers, including Suddle, of involvement in Murtaza's murder.
Zardari, who has been in a Karachi jail since his wife's dismissal, denies any part in his brother-in-law's death.
